title: Spring greens, lentil and spelt pot

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain whole food or a simple dairy staple, and vegetable stock is allowed.

supermarket.reason: Pearled spelt, Puy lentils and vegetarian hard cheese are all everyday lines at Tesco and other mainstream supermarkets.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only one large pan and a grater, and the techniques are simple softening and simmering.

works.reason: Spelt and Puy lentils (300g dry between them) in 1.2 litres of stock make a loose, brothy pot for four, and the 25-minute simmer suits both.

honest_times.reason: About 15 minutes of active work covers slicing the leeks, shredding the greens and softening, and the 25 plus 5 minutes of simmering matches the 30 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the thyme, lemon and chilli flakes, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm grain and lentil pot with 300g of spring greens suits a cold early-March lunch, and the greens are central.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lentils, wholegrain spelt, leeks and greens with a little crème fraîche and cheese make a filling, balanced meal.
